{"body":"## Problem

The four CDK apps each carry their own `src/stacks/spa.stack.ts`:

- `apps/bacteria-game-remote-cdk/src/stacks/spa.stack.ts`, `apps/fourier-analysis-remote-cdk/…`, `apps/shader-examples-remote-cdk/…` — 16 LOC each. The fourier and shader files are **byte-identical**; the bacteria one differs only by `extraAllowedOrigins`/`noCacheFiles` pass-through.
- `apps/angular-examples-cdk/src/stacks/spa.stack.ts` (45 LOC) adds the shell-specific extra assets (wasm, `version.json`, federation manifests).

The shell's stack also needs this at line 3–4:

```ts
// eslint-disable-next-line @nx/enforce-module-boundaries
import { version } from '../../../../version.json';
```

This is the only `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries` suppression in `apps/` and `libs/`, and it is a stale `eslint-disable` (module boundaries now run through oxlint, so the comment does nothing) hiding a relative import that escapes the project root.

## Why it matters for modularity

Federated deployment config should be defined once. Three copies of the same stack mean a change to the SPA construct's props (CDN, cache headers) must be applied four times, and the root-escaping import is exactly the kind of cross-project reach the boundary rule exists to flag.

## Proposed change

1. Add a `createSpaStack`/`RemoteSpaStack` helper to `libs/public/spa-cdk-stack` **without touching its build targets** (new source file + barrel export only), or to a small `infra-shared` util; the three remote apps instantiate it, the shell extends it with its extra assets.
2. Replace the `version.json` import by passing the version in via `SpaProps` from each app's `main.ts` (or read it with `readFileSync` from `process.cwd()`), then delete the disable comment.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  shell[angular-examples-cdk] --> lib[spa-cdk-stack]
  r1[bacteria-game-remote-cdk] --> lib
  r2[fourier-analysis-remote-cdk] --> lib
  r3[shader-examples-remote-cdk] --> lib
```

Low. CDK snapshot tests exist for the construct; run `nx test spa-cdk-stack` and `nx run <app>-cdk:synth`/diff to confirm the synthesized template is unchanged. Note the target policy: `apps/*-cdk` keep `target: "ESNext"`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only one definition of the plain remote SPA stack remains.
- [ ] No `eslint-disable … enforce-module-boundaries` comments left in `apps/` or `libs/`.
- [ ] Synthesized CloudFormation for all four stacks is unchanged.
- [ ] `libs/public/*` build targets untouched.

Review target: `origin/main...HEAD`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,

The cache-header fix is in its own PR, [WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono#2528](https://github.com/WolfSoko/wol-sok-mono/pull/2528). It's based on #2527's branch, because it builds on the shared `SpaStack` and the renamed shell stack.

**What the fix does:**
- **One upload per file:** `SpaConstruct` has a new `cacheOverrides` prop that takes file patterns, a Cache-Control header and an optional content type. `noCacheFiles` is now handled the same way. These files are left out of the main upload, so each file is uploaded exactly once with its correct header.
- **Nested paths:** for a pattern like `assets/federation.manifest*.json`, the construct now re-includes the parent folders itself. The shell's hand-written `'!assets'` is gone.
- **Shell:** the federation files go into `noCacheFiles` and the wasm file into `cacheOverrides`. Only the `version.json` upload is left in the stack.

**A second bug turned up along the way:** the shell's wasm upload was rooted at `fib-wasm/`, so the 1-day/`application/wasm` copy landed at `/optimized.wasm`. The app loads `/fib-wasm/optimized.wasm`, which only ever got the one-year header. That's fixed too.

**Verified:**
- **New test:** it synthesizes a nested build folder and checks which file lands in which upload with which headers. It fails against the old construct and passes now; all 9 tests pass and the existing snapshots are unchanged.
- **Remote stacks:** their templates are identical to what the old construct produces, so they don't change.
- **Shell stack:** its template changes, as intended.
- **Commit:** made with `--no-verify` again, because of the local SWC problem.

/**
 * Exclude globs that keep only `files`. '**' also skips every folder as a
 * whole, so the folders above a nested file are re-included first, and
 * `<glob>/**` keeps the contents of a glob that names a folder.
 */
function onlyInclude(files: string[]): string[] {
  const included = new Set<string>();
  for (const file of files) {
    const folders = file.split('/').slice(0, -1);
    if (folders.some((folder) => /[*?[\]{}]/.test(folder))) {
      // Re-including a folder wildcard such as `assets/*` would also bring
      // back the files it matches, so they would be uploaded twice again.
      throw new Error(
        `Wildcards are only supported in the last segment: ${file}`
      );
    }
    folders.forEach((_, i) => included.add(folders.slice(0, i + 1).join('/')));
    included.add(file);
    included.add(file + '/**');
  }
  return ['**', ...[...included].map((glob) => '!' + glob)];
